title: Binary GCD Algorithm for Integers or Bignums

problemStatement.plain: Can the binary GCD algorithm be extended to integers (handling negative inputs) or bignums.

currentState.focus: Integer half of OQ-02 closed in PR. Bignum half deferred.
currentState.nextAction: (Optional) Pursue Lehmer GCD or extended binary xgcd as separate follow-ups.

knowledge.progressSummary: ACT (completed integer half): Created proofs/Proofs/BinaryGcdOQ02.lean (~135 lines, 0 sorries, 0 axioms). Defines binaryGcdInt:ℤ→ℤ→ℕ via natAbs reduction; binaryGcdInt_eq_intGcd proves correctness vs Mathlib Int.gcd via two-line unfold + binaryGcd_eq_gcd. Sign invariance, edges, commutativity, divisibility universal property all derived through the bridge. Bignum half deferred (project-scale).
builtItems: Created Proofs/BinaryGcdOQ02.lean: binaryGcdInt definition + 13 theorems + 8 decide sanity examples (~135 lines)
binaryGcdInt_eq_intGcd : ∀ a b : ℤ, binaryGcdInt a b = Int.gcd a b — main correctness theorem
insights: binaryGcd:ℕ→ℕ→ℕ already defined at proofs/Proofs/GcdAlgorithmOQ02.lean:74 (with both-even/one-even/both-odd cases)
Mathlib has Int.gcd a b := a.natAbs.gcd b.natAbs — correct comparison target for integer extension
Integer extension is mechanical: binaryGcdInt a b := binaryGcd a.natAbs b.natAbs, prove correct via existing binaryGcd_correct + Int.gcd unfold (~50 lines)
Bignum extension is project-scale: would require formalizing bit-sequence representations (Nat.bits / Nat.digits 2) since Lean Nat is already unbounded — ~200+ lines for non-trivial reformulation
5 sibling files (BinaryGcdOQ01, OQ01OQ03, OQ01OQ04, OQ03, OQ03OQ01) all 0 sorries / 0 axioms — established formalization style available
Did not create OQ02 file this session due to no Docker availability — submitting unverified Int extension with surrogate sorry would be lower-value than a clear survey
The natAbs reduction is the canonical idiom for ℕ→ℤ extension of GCD-style algorithms; Mathlib Int.gcd uses the exact same pattern, so the bridge proof is two unfoldings
Marking sign-invariance as @[simp] makes downstream ℤ-level reasoning negation-blind without explicit case-splits
All algebraic properties (comm, divisibility, edges, self) inherit through the single bridge — each is one rewrite to the corresponding Int.gcd_* Mathlib lemma
Bignum half resolves automatically via Lean kernel: Nat ops compile to GMP, so binaryGcd already runs on bignums — formal bit-sequence proof is a separate project
